extraction.name: CommonsenseQA
extraction.description: A multiple-choice question answering dataset targeting commonsense knowledge, generated by extracting subgraphs from ConceptNet and having crowd workers author questions that discriminate between semantically similar target concepts. Contains 12,247 questions with 5 candidate answers each.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant (Tel-Aviv University and Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
extraction.citeAs: Talmor et al., 2019. CommonsenseQA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge. arXiv:1811.00937
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were generated by Amazon Mechanical Turk workers who were shown a source concept and three target concepts from ConceptNet and asked to author three multiple-choice questions (one per target concept), add two additional distractors per question, and verify question quality. Web snippets were also collected via Google search for each question-answer pair.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ConceptNet knowledge base (Speer et al., 2017), containing 32 million triplets with concepts and commonsense relations, and Google web search snippets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: ConceptNet triplets were filtered by: (1) removing general or well-explored relations, keeping 22 relations; (2) removing concepts longer than four words or not in English; (3) removing triplets where edit distance between source and target concept is too low. Questions failing verification (15%) were removed. Only annotators with at least 75% question pass rate were accepted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers authored three questions per ConceptNet subgraph (one per target concept), added two distractors per question (one chosen from ConceptNet, one manually authored), and were instructed to avoid surface clues. A separate group of workers verified question quality by choosing the correct answer or marking questions as unanswerable; each question was verified by 2 workers and only questions answered correctly by at least one verifier were kept.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question was verified by 2 workers; questions not answered correctly by at least one verifier were filtered out, removing 15% of questions. For human evaluation, 5 workers answered 100 sampled questions with majority vote, achieving 88.9% accuracy.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 verifiers per question; 5 workers for human evaluation
extraction.rai:dataBiases: 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions, indicating high annotator concentration. Questions may reflect annotation artifacts; the paper notes that benchmarks can allow models to exploit distributional biases rather than true understanding.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to English concepts from ConceptNet. Questions are generated from a subset of 22 ConceptNet relations, excluding general or well-explored ones. The random split is harder for models that memorize question-concept to answer mappings. Web snippets retrieved via Google search do not appear to carry sufficient useful information for reading comprehension models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of commonsense question answering models. The dataset is split 80/10/10 for train/development/test with both random and question-concept splits. Intended to evaluate and advance NLU systems on commonsense knowledge.
